text: "Follow your heart." "Just be happy." "You don't need to change."
You've heard these words your whole life. In movies, in songs, maybe even in church.
And a lot of people swear they're in the Bible.
But not one of them came from the mouth of Jesus. Some of them, He said the exact opposite.
In this video: six things Jesus never said, and what He said instead.
And at the end, you'll find out that Jesus Himself took what everyone was repeating, and put His word in its place. Six times, in the same sermon.
And the last one is the most dangerous, because almost everyone believes it.
If you want to hear the voice of Jesus, and not the voice of the world, subscribe right now. It's free, and it helps this message reach more people.
The first one is the most famous of all: "follow your heart."
It sounds beautiful. It sounds wise. The problem is what Jesus said about the heart.
One day, the religious leaders complained that the disciples were eating without washing their hands. To them, the dirt came from the outside.
Jesus answered: it's not what goes into the mouth that defiles a man. It's what comes out.
"For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, thefts, false witness."
He didn't say the heart is a guide. He said it's the source of the problem.
Centuries earlier, the prophet Jeremiah had already written: "The heart is deceitful above all things."
Notice: Jesus doesn't tell you to hate your heart. He tells you to stop obeying it, and to give it to the One who can make it new.
Tell me in the comments: how many times have you heard "follow your heart"? I read every single one.
The second one: "all that matters is being happy."
Now look at Jesus' last night with His disciples. He knew that in a few hours, He would be arrested.
And instead of promising them an easy life, He said:
"In the world ye shall have tribulation…"
"…but be of good cheer. I have overcome the world."
Jesus never sold a life without pain. He promised His presence in the middle of it.
The peace He offers isn't the absence of the storm. It's knowing who's in the boat with you.
And there's a detail in the Sermon on the Mount. Some translations begin the Beatitudes like this: "Happy are those who mourn."
Jesus wasn't against happiness. He just changed where it's found.

If even one of these lies has ever run your life, you're not alone. On this channel, every week there's a video like this one: what the world says, and what the Bible really says. Subscribe and turn on the bell, so you don't miss the next one.

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: The third one is quieter, but it runs a lot of lives: "only love those who love you."

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: Pay them back in their own coin. Whoever hurt you doesn't deserve a thing.

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus quoted a saying of His day: "Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy."

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: And He went on: "But I say unto you, love your enemies, and pray for them which persecute you."

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: Then He asked an uncomfortable question: "If ye love them which love you, what reward have ye?"

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: Loving the people who love you, anyone can do that. It doesn't take God.

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: Now the detail: the second half of that saying, "hate thine enemy," isn't in the Law. The Law only said to love your neighbour. The hate was a popular add-on.

sec: 3. "Only love those who love you" (Matt 5:43–46; Luke 23:34)
text: And Jesus didn't just teach it. On the cross, He prayed for the men nailing Him there: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do."
The fourth one is our generation's motto: "you have to have everything under control."
Spreadsheets, goals, plan B, plan C. And the anxiety at three in the morning, when none of it guarantees anything.
Jesus looked at the crowd and pointed to the sky: "Behold the fowls of the air: they sow not, neither do they reap, yet your heavenly Father feedeth them."
Then He asked: "Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?"
And He concluded: "Take no thought for the morrow. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof."
He didn't tell us to be irresponsible. He told us to stop carrying a day that hasn't even come yet.
Notice where this is: in the same sermon as the Lord's Prayer. "Give us this day our daily bread."
Not this month's bread. Today's. Even the prayer He taught takes tomorrow out of your hands.

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: The fifth one sounds like love: "you don't need to change. Just be yourself."

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: But do you know what Jesus' first public words were, in the Gospel of Mark?

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: "Repent ye, and believe the gospel." To repent is to change direction.

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: Later, He said: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me."

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: It's not "be yourself." It's "deny yourself."

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: But look at how He does it. They brought Him a woman caught in adultery, ready to stone her.

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: Jesus said: "Neither do I condemn thee." And then: "Go, and sin no more."

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: First the welcome. Then the change. Jesus accepts you as you are, but He loves you too much to leave you that way.

sec: 5. "You don't need to change" (Mark 1:15; Luke 9:23; John 8:11)
text: If you've made it this far, you're one of the few who watch to the end. And the last one is the most dangerous. If you haven't subscribed yet, now's the time.

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: The last one is the proudest: "you can do it on your own. You don't need anyone."

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: On the night He was betrayed, Jesus was walking with His disciples, and He talked about a vine.

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: "I am the vine, ye are the branches. Without me ye can do nothing."

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: Nothing. A branch that's been cut off doesn't get stronger. It dries up.

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: That night, one disciple thought he could. Peter said: "Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee."

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: Hours later, he denied Jesus three times. And the rooster crowed.

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: But the story doesn't end there. After the resurrection, on a beach, Jesus asked Peter: "Lovest thou me?"

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: Three times. One for each denial.

sec: 6. "You can do it on your own" (John 15:5; Matt 26:33–35; John 21:15–17)
text: The Peter who trusted in himself fell. The Peter who depended on Jesus preached to thousands.
Remember what I said at the beginning?
In the Sermon on the Mount, He said it six times: "Ye have heard that it was said… But I say unto you."
Six times, He took what everyone was repeating, and put His word in its place.
And He ended the sermon with a house.
"Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock."
The rain came down, the winds blew. And the house did not fall.
The world will keep repeating these lies. The question is which word you're building on.
